site.title: Little While
site.description: A Pomodoro focus and rest timer for iPhone.

apps.description:
Little While is a Pomodoro focus timer built around cycles of work and rest. Set your focus and break lengths, loop them automatically, follow the countdown from your Lock Screen, and see your focus time add up on a monthly calendar.

FOCUS + REST CYCLES
The Pomodoro method works because effort is paired with a real break. Set a focus block from 1 to 120 minutes and a rest period from 0 to 120 minutes. When focus ends, Little While alerts you and moves straight into rest, so the break is part of the plan instead of an afterthought.

AUTOMATIC LOOPS
Turn on Loop and the next focus block starts as soon as rest ends. Focus and rest repeat until you stop, and every completed cycle is counted, so a whole morning of deep work runs from a single tap.

A PAUSE THAT KEEPS YOU GOING
Pausing is intentionally short. A paused timer shows a one-minute countdown and then resumes on its own, so a quick interruption never quietly turns into an abandoned session. When you are truly done, stop the run and your progress is saved.

HISTORY AND CALENDAR
Every run is saved with its time, theme, progress, and completed cycles. A monthly calendar marks each day with a dot sized by how much you focused, and you can swipe back through past months to see your streaks. Delete any run you don't want to keep.

PLAYFUL THEMES
- Mr Smiles: a cheerful smiley face that bounces around your screen while you work. Grab him and flick him off the walls.
- He Loves Me: a hand-drawn daisy that drops its petals one by one as the minutes pass. He loves me... he loves me not.
Prefer to keep it simple? There's a minimal countdown too.

LOCK SCREEN AND DYNAMIC ISLAND
Live Activities show your remaining time and whether you are in focus or rest on the Lock Screen and in the Dynamic Island, so your phone can stay face down while you work.

ALERTS YOU WON'T MISS
On iOS 26 or later, Little While schedules system alarms for the end of each focus and rest period that sound even in Silent mode or a Focus, and you can dismiss them right from the alert. Otherwise it uses local notifications when permitted.

PRIVATE BY DESIGN
No account, ads, analytics, or tracking. Your settings and history stay on your device.

Includes VoiceOver support, adjustable duration controls, and Reduce Motion support.

Requires iOS 18 or later.
apps.name: Little While
apps.notes:
Hi, thanks for taking another look at Little While. There's no account or sign-in and nothing needs a network connection. Please allow the notification and alarm prompts when they come up, otherwise you won't hear the end-of-timer alerts.

Little While is a Pomodoro timer, so the whole idea is working in cycles: a focus block, then a break, then another focus block. Here's how to see the main features.

Focus and rest: tap the sliders button in the top left to open Settings. Set Focus and Rest with the two dials (rest can be 0 if you just want a single timer) and tap Start. I'd suggest 1 min focus and 1 min rest so you're not waiting around. When focus ends you get an alert and it goes right into the rest period.

Looping: in Settings, turn on Loop before you hit Start. When rest ends the next focus block starts on its own, and it keeps going until you tap stop (top right). History shows how many cycles you got through.

Pause: this one is on purpose so I want to call it out. If you pause a running timer it doesn't stay paused forever. You get a one minute "Resuming in" countdown and then it starts back up by itself. The point of a Pomodoro is to not lose the cycle, and in my experience a paused timer usually just gets forgotten. You can tap play to resume early or stop to end the run.

Themes: the theme picker is at the top of Settings. Mr Smiles is a little smiley face that bounces around the screen while you work, and you can grab him and flick him around. He Loves Me is a daisy that drops a petal at a time as the timer runs down.

History: the clock button in the top left opens History. There's a month calendar at the top where each day's dot gets bigger the more you focused that day (use the arrows or swipe to change months), and your past runs are listed underneath. Swipe left on an old run to delete it.

Lock Screen: once a timer is running, lock the phone or go to the Home Screen and you'll see the countdown on the Lock Screen, and in the Dynamic Island on phones that have one. It also shows whether you're in focus or rest.

Alarms: on iOS 26 and up the end-of-period alerts use AlarmKit, so they go off even in Silent mode or a Focus. On older versions it falls back to regular notifications.

A couple of small things: the History and Settings buttons hide while a run is going so you're not tempted to fiddle with it, just stop the run to get them back. You can also long press the play button to start over. The privacy policy link is at the bottom of Settings.

Thanks!
Graham
